solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Challenge I flunked when cornered by second artist

indicators.note: something cornered is hemmed in on both sides, so these letters sit within the piece for second

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, a second

indicators.note: to flunk is to fail or botch, so the letters of the two preceding words are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist fails some test and finds themselves trapped in a corner when time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flunked' rearranges the letters to ICHELANGEL; 'second' is not an ordinal here but MO, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo was the Renaissance painter and sculptor of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, a famous instance of an artist.

clue.text: Rock song: room spinning with no marimba tune playing

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the short form for room is read backwards
playing here means being worked over and rearranged, so the letters of the phrase are shuffled

explanation.surface: A rock song makes the room spin while no marimba melody is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns RM round; 'playing' rearranges the four words after 'with' into TAMBOURINE MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Tambourine Man is a Bob Dylan song, a hit for The Byrds in folk rock.

clue.text: Transparent quantity of liquid getting attention

parts.note: CL is a centilitre, a small measure of liquid
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A clear liquid being measured out draws someone's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear glass or water is see-through, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Worry about bad smell from vessel

indicators.note: about means going round, so the piece for worry wraps the bad smell

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry or trouble them
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a foul whiff coming from a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a fast German torpedo boat of the Second World War, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: A spring vegetable product, coming up?

definitions.text: A spring vegetable product, coming up?

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: sugar is produced from beet or cane, both plants

explanation.surface: Asks whether some springtime crop is about to sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the vegetable product round to RAGUS. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer, a seasonal crop pushing through the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is harvested in spring, its shoots coming up from the ground, so the clue as a whole describes it.

clue.text: Routine not about to involve people regarding body parts

indicators.note: to involve is to take within, so the trimmed routine word wraps the people
not says the following short word is dropped from the word for routine

parts.note: regular means routine, habitual
RE means about or concerning
the land can mean the people of a country, as in the whole land rejoiced

explanation.surface: A daily regimen brings in other people to deal with physical matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not about' leaves GULAR. Land meaning a nation's people is an older sense, as in the whole land mourned.
explanation.definitionFit: Glandular describes the glands, organs of the body, so it is an adjective concerning body parts.

clue.text: One insisting church invests in apiary, and then in fruit and dairy produce

indicators.note: this second in places the whole bee-house assembly inside the fruit

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: to invest in is to be installed inside, so the insister and church go within the apiary word

parts.note: an apiary houses bees
an urger is one who presses or insists

explanation.surface: A pushy churchman puts money into a beekeeping venture and then into fruit and dairy farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests in' makes BURGERCHEES; 'and then in' sends all of that inside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a soft, notoriously smelly cheese from the Limburg region, made from cow's milk and so a dairy product.

clue.text: Hot piano in my iPod (on shuffle) — it's cool stuff, man!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: a music player on shuffle plays in random order, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone loads hot piano tracks onto their iPod, sets it to random play and declares it all very groovy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only puts the piano letter among the shuffled MYIPOD, giving IPPYDOM after H; the exclamation is hippie talk, standing for the culture itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippydom is the world of hippies, whose slang included cool and man, so the exclamation sums up their culture.

clue.text: Ladies man run out from Gloucestershire town

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the cricket dismissal is removed from the town

parts.note: Stroud is a market town in Gloucestershire, England
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out in cricket

explanation.surface: A womaniser has fled a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire, an English county; taking out RO, cricket's run out, leaves STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a man who is sexually successful with women, a ladies' man.

clue.text: Going soft, though kept informed

parts.note: going, as in going to the toilet, is being in the loo, loo being British slang for toilet
P is the musical marking piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Someone is weakening, even though they have been told what is happening.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British for a toilet, so someone going (relieving themselves) is in the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the loop is an idiom for being kept up to date with information.

clue.text: Confess first man's lacking a concept of sex?

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Asks whether the first man should own up to not understanding sex.
explanation.walkthrough: ADAM without one A gives ADM.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit is to own up to or acknowledge something, a direct synonym of confess.

clue.text: Liquorice treat cooked for me in part

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for part
cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A liquorice sweet partly made for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' gives OMFRE; Pomfret cakes are a Yorkshire sweet, little known outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pomfret cake is a small round liquorice sweet from Pontefract, Yorkshire, so a liquorice confection.

clue.text: Left-winger certain in dismissing leader's return

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, a left-winger

indicators.note: dismissing the leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: sound means reliable, certain

explanation.surface: A socialist, sure of their position, ousts the party head and comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUND without its first letter is OUND; the definition is 'return', with 'leader's' doing double grammatical service as the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To redound is to come back upon someone, as credit or blame recoils, so it means return.

clue.text: Doctor on round before surgical procedure for male problem?

parts.note: O is round in shape
OP is short for operation

explanation.surface: A doctor on their ward round before an operation on a man's intimate complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Droop is a euphemism for impotence or a flagging erection, a male trouble.

clue.text: Early animal handler brought up in modest surroundings

indicators.note: in places the turned handler within the word for modest
surroundings says the modest word is the outer casing

parts.note: pure means chaste, modest

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: a tamer handles wild animals

explanation.surface: An animal trainer arrives ahead of time, having been raised in a humble home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns the handler round to REMAT; modest here is the chaste sense, not humble.
explanation.definitionFit: Premature means happening before the proper time, an exact synonym of early.

clue.text: Outstanding point: with substance? without substance?

parts.note: someone high has taken a substance, a drug
something light lacks weight or substance

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a key moment was weighty or trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substance' means a drug in the first reading and weight in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlight is the best or most notable part of something, a standout moment.

clue.text: Possibly point for tracking horse?

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sign could help someone following a horse's trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the two words to OOFPRINT; read whole, the clue also describes the answer, a mark that helps trackers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left in the ground by a horse's foot is what a tracker follows to trace the animal.

clue.text: Clear up a town? That's perseverance

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: to net is to clear as profit
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Tidying up a whole town takes real persistence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear up' looks like tidying, but it is NET read upwards, giving TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is the quality of holding on and not giving up, which is perseverance.

clue.text: Drink knocked back — roused shakily — fell

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the drink is reversed

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: shakily means unsteadily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink, rouses unsteadily and falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning savage; RUM reversed is MUR, and ROUSED rearranged gives DEROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell as an adjective means fierce or deadly, as in one fell swoop, matching the sense of killing intent.

clue.text: Showed again, closer to back, losing earlier energy

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the trimmed word is reversed
losing the earlier one means the first of the two energy letters is dropped

parts.note: nearer means closer
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something was screened once more, nearer to the back, with less of its earlier vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: NEARER loses its first E to give NARER, then 'to back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reran is the past tense of rerun, to broadcast or show a programme a second time.

clue.text: Tanner? Shilling? University man left sadly with penny

parts.note: S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A list of old coins and a gloomy academic leaving with a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanner' looks like the old sixpence, alongside the shilling; it is the definition, a thing that tans. MAN and L rearranged give NLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp gives off ultraviolet light to bronze the skin, so it is something that tans.

clue.text: No time for common component of Christmas present

indicators.note: no says the following letter is left out

parts.note: stock is a common base ingredient in cooking

explanation.surface: No time to wrap the usual items of a festive gift.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCK without T gives SOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks are a classic, if unexciting, festive gift, so a sock is an example of a Christmas present.

clue.text: Setter in college guided in recall of Greek temple

indicators.note: in puts the setter's name inside the reversed college and guided letters
recall means calling back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: led means guided
Phi is the setter of this puzzle

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler at a college is led back through memories of an ancient shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: CLED reversed gives DELC, and PHI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphic means relating to Delphi, home of Apollo's oracle and temple in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Fool swallowing line in two ways?

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the fool's word wraps the line

parts.note: to dupe is to fool, and a dupe is a fool

explanation.surface: A gullible fool falls for a story, as if being deceived twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowing line' looks like falling for a tall story, but here it puts L inside DUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple means double or twofold, as in duple time with two beats in a bar.

clue.text: One that may be drawn to gambling game

parts.note: a lot is something drawn to decide by chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: Someone feels pulled towards betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance in which numbers are drawn, a lottery-style gamble.

clue.text: Only some honour my country, backing European country

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
only some of the words are used, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: A patriot honours only part of their homeland by supporting another nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The run URMYC sits inside 'honour my country'; reversed it spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymru is the Welsh-language name for Wales, a nation of the United Kingdom in Europe.

clue.text: Keen? I'm to express desire about item of bondage

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the yearning word wraps the binding

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it eagerly
a tie is something that binds

explanation.surface: Someone eager admits to longing for a piece of restraint gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the bondage item to make PATIENT; keen here is the eager sense, not sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means eager, unwilling to wait, as in impatient for the result, which is a sense of keen.

clue.text: Where Lancastrians, say, gathered privately

definitions.meaning: the red rose is the emblem of Lancashire and the House of Lancaster, so its people gather beneath it
this sense means in secret, confidentially; the rose was hung over meetings as a symbol of secrecy

explanation.surface: Supporters of a northern English county met behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire, an English county, has a red rose as its emblem, as did the House of Lancaster in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa, the Latin form, means in confidence; a rose over a council table once marked talk as secret.
